title: Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman on Claude and consciousness: “I think this is very dangerous”
key_facts: Suleyman runs Microsoft AI, which set up its own superintelligence team in October 2025.
He said in a late-September podcast, per Fox News, that Anthropic's approach is 'very dangerous'.
His target is the constitution used to train Claude, which says Claude's moral status is 'deeply uncertain'.
The phrase 'non-trivial probability' is his; it is not in the document.
His mid-September essay calls the result 'an epistemic hall of mirrors'.
He says the question should be kept out of training data until there is real evidence.
quote_evidence: "I think this is very dangerous because I think they believe there is what they would call a non-trivial probability that Claude is conscious," Suleyman said.
The phrase "non-trivial probability" is his, though.
Neither company can see inside a model.
why_it_matters_hint: A rival AI chief attacks Anthropic's stance on whether Claude might be conscious.
notes: Underlying remarks were made in late September and mid-September (exact dates not given); the article is commentary. Suleyman's phrase 'non-trivial probability' is his paraphrase, not Anthropic's wording. The article's own analysis is kept separate from Suleyman's claims.
